name: Spare Studio
replaces: Adobe Creative Cloud: Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, InCopy, Premiere Pro, Media Encoder, After Effects, Lightroom, Lightroom Classic, Acrobat, Acrobat Sign, Audition, XD, Animate, Character Animator, Fresco, Bridge, Dreamweaver, Express, Firefly, Substance 3D, Dimension, Adobe Fonts, Adobe Stock, Frame.io and Behance
summary: One creative suite for photos, vectors, layout, video, motion, raw photos, PDF, audio, screens, animation and 3D, built on one shared studio core and the Spareware kit. Free to use, open formats, AI optional and at cost, and owned by its members.

areas.name: Accounts, membership, teams and admin
areas.summary: How a person or an organisation starts, signs in, joins the co-op, pays for the few things that cost money and manages people and machines. Replaces the Creative Cloud account, plans and Admin Console. Every app works without an account; an account adds sync, sharing, AI at cost and buying from Spare Market.

features.name: Install the suite and start without an account
features.does: Download one installer, pick the apps they want and start working offline with no sign-in.

parts.name: Installers on the shared desktop shell
parts.what: Studio's app picker on signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux that add or remove single apps; the installer belongs in the kit's shared desktop shell, used by Spare Arch and Spare Office too.

parts.name: Browser build study
parts.what: Whether the heavy apps can run in a browser on WebAssembly and WebGPU: memory limits, speed, file access, and which apps are worth it.

parts.name: Studio update channels
parts.what: Studio's update channels with pause, skip and roll back, on the kit's update delivery.

parts.name: Local profile without an account
parts.what: Preferences, recent files and libraries kept on the device until the person chooses to sign in.

features.name: Make a Spareware account and sign in
features.does: Create one Spareware login with a passkey or password, use it in every app and on every device, and get back in if they lose access.

parts.name: Studio sign-in
parts.what: The kit's passkey-first sign-in, recovery and new sign-in alerts inside every Studio app, with device sign-in codes for shared and lab machines.

parts.name: The studio as a sign-in client
parts.what: The apps sign in through the accounts service's OpenID Connect flow and keep tokens in the system keychain.

features.name: Find their way on the first day
features.does: See a short welcome, say what they make, and get starter templates and a guided first edit.

parts.name: Suite home screen
parts.what: One start screen with recent files, new-document presets, templates and the installed apps.

parts.name: Studio first-run tours
parts.what: A skippable tour per app on a real sample file, on the kit's first-run guide.

parts.name: Guides for people moving from other tools
parts.what: Plain notes and optional shortcut sets that map common habits onto our tools, written in our own words.

parts.name: Learning centre
parts.what: Searchable how-to articles and short videos inside each app, also available offline.

parts.name: Sample files the co-op owns
parts.what: Photos, footage, sound and layouts made or licensed by the co-op for tutorials and templates.

features.name: Join the co-op and have a say
features.does: Become a member, read Spare Studio's proposals and vote on the matters Studio's members decide.

parts.name: Join from the studio
parts.what: A link from every Studio app into the kit's join flow, which ties the account to a co-op membership and its share.

parts.name: Studio proposals and votes
parts.what: Studio's proposal types, such as the free allowance, the AI policy, at-cost prices and the order of apps, on the kit's proposals and ballots, with results applied as operations.

parts.name: Spare Studio's electorate
parts.what: States who votes on Studio matters; lean: every co-op member who uses Spare Studio votes on the free allowance, the AI policy, at-cost prices and the order of apps, since Studio has no workers in the marketplace sense, and asset sellers vote on the market fee in Spare Market.

features.name: Pay only for what costs money
features.does: Set a monthly cap for cloud storage, co-op-hosted AI and video processing, pay after use, and see what each dollar paid for.

parts.name: Per-member usage meter
parts.what: Counts storage, AI compute, video processing and server jobs per member against their cap; it belongs in the kit beside the per-app usage metering, since Spare Office, Spare Social and Spare Arch need the same.

parts.name: Monthly cap and pay after use
parts.what: Lets a person set a monthly cap and pay for use after each month through the payment provider, in their own currency; the co-op never holds a prepaid balance.

parts.name: Studio tax invoices
parts.what: Monthly tax invoices and receipts for at-cost Studio charges, issued through the kit's tax invoices.

parts.name: Studio lines on the open ledger
parts.what: Studio's costs for storage, AI compute and video processing, and how each at-cost price was set, on the kit's ledger pages.

parts.name: Free allowance and hardship rule
parts.what: A free storage and AI allowance per member, with a published rule for people who cannot pay.

parts.name: Tax on services sold overseas
parts.what: Which GST, VAT and digital services tax the co-op owes on at-cost storage and AI sold to people overseas, when it must register in each country, and how remote services rules treat marketplaces; the rules belong in the kit's tax rules per country.

parts.name: Failed jobs and charge disputes
parts.what: Charges nothing, or refunds automatically, for paid jobs that fail, are cancelled or are blocked by safety checks, and lets a member dispute any usage charge through the kit's support cases.

features.name: Manage their account and data
features.does: Change details, see signed-in devices, download all their data and delete the account.

parts.name: Studio settings and privacy choices
parts.what: Studio's own choices, such as AI tools, training consent and cloud sync, on the kit's settings and connected apps pages.

parts.name: Studio files in the data export
parts.what: Adds every cloud file, library, comment and version history, in open formats, to the kit's data export.

parts.name: Delete the account and its files
parts.what: Deletes the account and its cloud files through the kit's account deletion, keeping only the records the law requires, such as tax invoices, signed documents and market sales, and keeping buyers' licences to assets they bought.

features.name: Set up a team, school or business
features.does: Create an organisation, invite people, give them roles, share libraries and storage, and keep the work when people leave.

parts.name: Studio roles for organisations
parts.what: Studio's permissions, such as editing shared libraries, publishing and paid AI, as roles on the kit's organisation model.

parts.name: Single sign-on for organisations
parts.what: Sign-in through an organisation's own identity system using OpenID Connect or SAML; it belongs in the kit beside the organisation model, since Spare Office needs it too.

parts.name: Studio usage on organisation bills
parts.what: Splits an organisation's at-cost Studio usage by team on the kit's business accounts, with purchase orders and invoices.

parts.name: Schools and classes
parts.what: Class spaces where teachers hand out and collect work, with student accounts the school manages.

parts.name: Hand-over when someone leaves
parts.what: When a person leaves an organisation, the organisation's cloud files, libraries and share links they owned pass to the organisation, and their personal files stay with them.

parts.name: Domain claiming and account provisioning
parts.what: Lets an organisation claim its email domain and create, change and remove accounts automatically through the SCIM standard; it belongs in the kit with directory sync.

features.name: Run the suite on many computers
features.does: Install, set up and update the apps on many machines and set policies such as AI off.

parts.name: Silent install and managed updates
parts.what: Installer options and update channels that IT staff push with standard device-management tools.

parts.name: Organisation policies
parts.what: Settings an admin can lock, such as AI tools off, no sharing outside the organisation, or a storage region.

parts.name: Admin audit log
parts.what: Every admin change recorded as an operation the organisation can read; it belongs in the kit beside the organisation model, since Spare Office needs it too.

parts.name: AI, agent and plugin policies
parts.what: Lets an admin allow only listed plugins, allow or block outside AI agents and MCP access, and choose which AI providers people may use.

features.name: Use the apps in a browser
features.does: Open and edit files in a web browser with nothing to install, without losing work kept there.

parts.name: Browser version
parts.what: The apps the study finds workable, compiled to WebAssembly and served as an installable web app.

parts.name: Browser storage safety
parts.what: Handles storage quotas and eviction, file access that only some browsers allow, phone memory limits and an offline service worker, and reminds people to export work kept only in the browser.

parts.name: Browser accessibility mirror
parts.what: A hidden page structure that mirrors canvas content for screen readers in the browser build, in the kit's shared interface components with Spare Office's canvas mirror.

areas.name: Studio core: workspace, documents and history
areas.summary: The shared base every app stands on: one workspace, one document model where every edit is a non-destructive operation, an open file format, smooth handling of huge files and history that never loses work. Built once, used by every Spare Studio app.

features.name: Work in one familiar workspace
features.does: Arrange panels, tools and saved workspaces, and move between apps without learning a new layout.

parts.name: App shell
parts.what: The frame every app shares: header, tool bar, panels, canvas and status line, following the Spareware design guide.

parts.name: Panels and saved workspaces
parts.what: Docked, floating and tabbed panels, with saved layouts for each kind of task.

parts.name: Tool system
parts.what: One way to define tools, their options and their on-canvas handles, shared by every app.

parts.name: Shortcuts and command search
parts.what: Every command searchable by name, with shortcut sets a person can edit, export and share.

parts.name: Preferences
parts.what: Settings per app and for the whole suite, stored as data the person can export.

parts.name: Canvas view
parts.what: Zoom, pan, rotate, rulers, guides, grids and several views of one document.

features.name: Start a document the right size
features.does: Pick a preset for print, screen, social, video or phone, or set their own size, units and resolution.

parts.name: Document presets
parts.what: Sizes for paper (ISO and US), screens, social formats and video, with A4 and metric units first in New Zealand.

parts.name: New document screen
parts.what: Choose a preset or a custom size, colour mode, bit depth and background.

features.name: Build with layers, groups, masks and artboards
features.does: Stack content in layers and groups, mask it, and keep several artboards or pages in one file.

parts.name: Studio document model
parts.what: One model for layers, groups, masks, artboards, pages and timelines that every app uses.

parts.name: Non-destructive edit graph
parts.what: Adjustments, filters and effects stored as live operations that can be changed or removed at any time.

parts.name: Linked and embedded content
parts.what: Place other files as live links or embedded copies, update or relink them when they move, and replace them.

parts.name: Layers panel
parts.what: Shows, orders, groups, locks, hides, colour-labels and searches layers in every app.

features.name: Undo anything and step through history
features.does: Undo and redo every change, jump back through the history list and branch from an older state.

parts.name: Undo and redo on the operation log
parts.what: Undo built on the kit's operation log, so people, scripts and AI share one history.

parts.name: History panel and snapshots
parts.what: A list of every step, named snapshots, and branching from any earlier step.

features.name: Save in an open format and never lose work
features.does: Save to a documented open file any tool can read, with autosave and recovery after a crash or power cut.

parts.name: Project file container
parts.what: Whether studio files use a SQLite container or a custom chunk file, shared with Spare Arch's decision.

parts.name: Spare Studio file format
parts.what: A documented, layered, open file format with a published schema and test files.

parts.name: Format reader and writer library
parts.what: A library that reads and writes the format, published so other tools can use it too.

parts.name: Public format specification
parts.what: Plain documentation of the format with examples, version rules and a validator.

parts.name: Autosave and crash recovery
parts.what: Saves work continuously in the background and restores it after a crash or power cut.

features.name: Open and save common image files
features.does: Open and export PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, TIFF, GIF, HEIF, BMP, OpenRaster and SVG files, including HDR photos from phones.

parts.name: Image codecs
parts.what: Readers and writers for common raster formats using permissively licensed libraries.

parts.name: HEIF and HEVC patent check
parts.what: Whether reading and writing HEIF photos needs a patent licence and whether platform codecs avoid it, as part of the one engine-media codec study.

parts.name: SVG import and export
parts.what: Reads and writes SVG with layers, text and gradients kept editable where possible.

parts.name: Metadata kept through every edit
parts.what: Reads and writes EXIF, IPTC and XMP metadata and keeps it through edits and exports.

parts.name: HDR photos with gain maps
parts.what: Opens phone HDR photos with their gain maps (ISO 21496-1) and exports HDR JPEG, AVIF and JPEG XL with gain maps.

features.name: Open files from the tools we replace
features.does: Open layered PSD and PSB files and illustration files through the PDF inside them.

parts.name: What we may legally read and write
parts.what: Each Adobe format checked against a published specification, with links.

parts.name: PSD and PSB reader and writer
parts.what: Reads and writes layered PSD and PSB files from Adobe's published specification, keeping layers, masks and text.

parts.name: Illustration files through their PDF
parts.what: Opens illustration files by reading only the PDF they embed.

parts.name: EPS and PostScript study
parts.what: Whether to write a PostScript interpreter from the published specification or read only the preview and PDF inside EPS files, since Ghostscript is AGPL.

parts.name: Import report
parts.what: Lists anything that could not be brought across exactly and what it became instead.

parts.name: PSD fidelity study
parts.what: How exactly layers, masks, effects and text layers can round-trip through PSD and PSB from the published specification, tested on real files.

features.name: Edit huge files smoothly
features.does: Work on very large images, long documents and long timelines without waiting.

parts.name: Renderer approach
parts.what: Our own renderer on wgpu or a web renderer first, shared with Spare Arch's decision.

parts.name: GPU image pipeline
parts.what: Tiles, filters, blending and adjustments as GPU compute on wgpu with a CPU fallback, built on engine-render as one image pipeline that the photo editors in Spare Social, Spare Market and Spare OS can use too.

parts.name: Tile and page cache
parts.what: Loads only what is on screen at the zoom in use and pages the rest from disk.

parts.name: Speed benchmarks
parts.what: A public set of very large test files with timings checked on every change.

features.name: Keep and compare versions
features.does: Name versions, see what changed between them and restore any of them.

parts.name: Named versions
parts.what: Versions kept on the operation log, locally and in sync.

parts.name: Visual compare
parts.what: Side-by-side and overlay compare of two versions with the changed areas marked.

features.name: Get help in context
features.does: Hover any tool for a short tip, read the manual offline, ask other members and report a problem from inside the app.

parts.name: Instant tips
parts.what: A short tip on every tool and setting that shows at once on hover.

parts.name: Offline manual
parts.what: The full manual for every app, shipped with the app and searchable.

parts.name: Studio in the member forum
parts.what: A link from every app to a Spare Studio section of the kit's member forum.

parts.name: Studio crash and bug reports
parts.what: Sends crash and bug reports with consent through the kit's crash reports, with the person's file content stripped out.

features.name: Run long jobs in the background
features.does: Export, render and batch-process in the background while they keep working, and see progress, pause or cancel.

parts.name: Shared job queue
parts.what: One background queue for exports, renders and batch runs in every app, with progress, cancel, watch folders and limits on processor and graphics use.

features.name: Record and repeat steps
features.does: Record a set of steps once and replay it on other files in any app.

parts.name: Action recorder
parts.what: Records operations as a replayable script in the studio core, shared by every app, and runs it on many files through the job queue.

features.name: Open EPS and PostScript files
features.does: Open old EPS and PostScript artwork and edit it.

parts.name: EPS and PostScript import
parts.what: Reads EPS and PostScript using the approach the study chose, without GPL or AGPL interpreters.

areas.name: Type, colour and output
areas.summary: The shared core for text in every app, colour that stays true from screen to print and video, and output to printers, files and the web, with proof of where a file came from. Replaces the type, colour and export features spread across every Adobe app.

features.name: Set type in any app
features.does: Add and style text with any installed or open font, including OpenType features and variable fonts.

parts.name: Text engine libraries
parts.what: Recommended open libraries for fonts, shaping and layout, with licences, and what Spare Layout needs on top.

parts.name: Text engine
parts.what: Font loading, shaping, bidirectional text, line breaking and paragraph layout, built in engine-text and shared with Spare Arch and Spare Office.

parts.name: Text layers and frames
parts.what: Point text, area text, text on a path and threaded frames as one shared text object.

parts.name: Character and paragraph panels
parts.what: Size, leading, tracking, kerning, OpenType features and variable font axes.

parts.name: Missing font handling
parts.what: Finds missing fonts, offers open replacements and keeps the original font names in the file.

parts.name: Colour and emoji fonts
parts.what: Draws COLR v1, SVG-in-OpenType and sbix colour fonts, so emoji and colour type work in every app.

features.name: Write well in many languages
features.does: Type in any script with any input method, with spelling checks, hyphenation and the right line breaks for that language.

parts.name: Complex scripts
parts.what: Arabic, Hebrew, Indic, Thai and CJK shaping, vertical text, ruby and Japanese spacing rules.

parts.name: Spelling and hyphenation dictionaries
parts.what: Open dictionaries per language, te reo Māori and English (New Zealand) first, each licence checked, kept in engine-text so Spare Office, Spare OS and Spare Arch use the same ones.

parts.name: Glyphs, macrons and smart quotes
parts.what: A glyph panel, easy macron input and smart quotes that follow each language's rules.

parts.name: Input methods for canvas text
parts.what: IME composition and candidate windows, dead keys and compose keys for text drawn on the GPU canvas, on desktop and in the browser; built in engine-text with Spare Office and Spare Arch.

features.name: See true colour on screen
features.does: Work in sRGB, Display P3, wide-gamut RGB, CMYK, Lab and HDR, with colour-managed screens.

parts.name: Colour management approach
parts.what: How open tools manage colour, their licences, and a recommended approach for print, photo and video.

parts.name: Colour management engine
parts.what: ICC profile transforms for photo and print, and OpenColorIO for video and film, on the GPU.

parts.name: Screen profiles and HDR display
parts.what: Reads each screen's profile and shows HDR content correctly where the screen supports it.

parts.name: Colour modes and bit depths
parts.what: RGB, CMYK, greyscale, Lab and multichannel at 8, 16 and 32 bits per channel.

parts.name: Screen calibration options
parts.what: How members can calibrate screens with common measuring devices without GPL or AGPL code.

features.name: Pick, mix and keep colours
features.does: Pick colours, build palettes and harmonies, sample from images and check contrast.

parts.name: Colour picker and mixer
parts.what: Wheel, sliders and number fields in every colour mode, with an eyedropper that samples anywhere on screen.

parts.name: Palettes and harmonies
parts.what: Builds colour harmonies and pulls palettes from images.

parts.name: Contrast checker
parts.what: Checks text and background colours against accessibility contrast rules.

parts.name: Spot colour books
parts.what: Lets people use spot colour books they hold a licence for, and checks which books the co-op may ship.

features.name: Proof for print before printing
features.does: Soft-proof against a press or printer profile and see the colours that will not print.

parts.name: Soft proof and gamut warning
parts.what: Simulates the output profile on screen and marks areas that fall outside it.

parts.name: Separations and ink preview
parts.what: Shows each ink plate, total ink coverage and overprints.

features.name: Print from any app
features.does: Print to home, office and photo printers with colour management, bleed, marks and tiling.

parts.name: Print screen
parts.what: System printing with page setup, scaling, tiling, crop marks and bleed.

parts.name: Printer colour handling
parts.what: Sends colour-managed output or lets the printer manage colour, with the choice explained in plain words.

features.name: Export for screen, print and social
features.does: Export a document, page, artboard, layer or selection in many formats and sizes at once.

parts.name: Export pipeline
parts.what: One export engine for images, PDF, SVG and stills, with saved presets.

parts.name: Export screen
parts.what: Choose formats, sizes, quality and file names, with a preview of quality and file size.

parts.name: Export many at once
parts.what: Exports every artboard, page or layer in several sizes in one go.

parts.name: Print-ready PDF
parts.what: PDF/X output with bleed, marks and embedded fonts for commercial printers.

features.name: Prove where a file came from
features.does: Attach content credentials that record how a file was made and edited, including any AI use, and choose what they reveal.

parts.name: Content credentials
parts.what: Signs exported files with C2PA content credentials, using a signer that belongs in engine-media and is shared with Spare Social.

parts.name: Credentials viewer
parts.what: Shows the content credentials on any file opened in the studio, using the shared reader in engine-media.

parts.name: Signing certificates and conformance
parts.what: How the co-op gets, stores and rotates the certificates that sign content credentials, and joins the C2PA conformance programme and trust list, once for Spare Studio and Spare Social.

parts.name: Credential privacy choices
parts.what: A choice on each export to leave the name, the edit history or the location out of content credentials.

areas.name: Spare Library: assets, fonts, colours and templates
areas.summary: One browser for every file, shared libraries that work in every app, open fonts, open stock and templates, and a door into Spare Market for the assets members sell. Replaces Bridge, Creative Cloud Libraries, Adobe Fonts, Adobe Stock and Adobe Color. Selling, orders, tax and payouts for assets live in Spare Market on the shared marketplace engine.

features.name: Browse and find any file
features.does: Browse folders, preview every supported format, filter by metadata and search by content.

parts.name: Asset browser
parts.what: A fast browser with thumbnails and previews for images, raw photos, vectors, video, audio, PDF and 3D.

parts.name: Thumbnail and preview builder
parts.what: Builds and caches previews for every supported format in the background.

parts.name: Search and filters
parts.what: Search by name, metadata, colour and keywords, and optionally by what is in the picture.

parts.name: Batch rename and metadata editing
parts.what: Renames many files by pattern and edits metadata in bulk.

features.name: Keep reusable libraries
features.does: Save colours, text styles, graphics, brushes and components to a library and use them in every app.

parts.name: Library data model
parts.what: One open format for colours, styles, graphics, brushes, components and templates.

parts.name: Libraries panel
parts.what: Drag items into and out of libraries in every app.

parts.name: Shared and synced libraries
parts.what: Libraries synced across devices and shared with a team, updating every place an item is used.

features.name: Keep work on brand
features.does: Lock an organisation's logos, colours, fonts and templates so everyone's work stays on brand.

parts.name: Brand kits
parts.what: Logos, colours, fonts and templates an organisation locks so everyone's work stays on brand.

features.name: Use and manage fonts
features.does: Find open-licence fonts, turn them on in every app and see what each font's licence allows.

parts.name: Open font catalogue
parts.what: A catalogue of fonts under open licences such as the SIL Open Font License, with previews and pairings, kept in engine-text so Spare Office, Spare OS and Spare Arch share one.

parts.name: Font manager
parts.what: Turns fonts on and off across apps, groups them and shows their licence terms.

parts.name: Font licence rules
parts.what: What each font licence allows for embedding in PDF, packaging for print and use on the web.

features.name: Start from a template
features.does: Start any kind of project from a co-op-made template and make it their own.

parts.name: Template gallery
parts.what: Co-op-made templates for posters, social posts, documents, slides, video and more.

parts.name: Licence for templates and samples
parts.what: A stated licence that lets members use co-op templates and sample files in commercial work.

features.name: Find free images, footage and sound
features.does: Search open-licence stock from inside every app, with licence and credit added automatically.

parts.name: Open media search
parts.what: Searches open-licence collections whose terms allow it, recording each item's licence and credit.

parts.name: Stock source terms
parts.what: Each source's licence and API terms checked before it is connected.

parts.name: Licence and credit tracking
parts.what: Keeps each placed asset's licence and credit with the file and lists them on export.

features.name: Buy and install assets from Spare Market
features.does: Browse brushes, fonts, templates, photos, footage, sounds and plugins that members sell in Spare Market, and install what they buy straight into a library.

parts.name: Spare Market in the library
parts.what: Browses Spare Market's digital goods and installs bought assets into a library through Market's public API; listings, orders, tax and payouts stay in Spare Market on kit-market.

parts.name: Asset licences kept with files
parts.what: Keeps each bought asset's licence and the buyer's licence certificate with the file and lists them on export.

parts.name: Sell from a library
parts.what: Sends an asset from a Studio library to a Spare Market listing with watermarked previews, version updates and any model and property releases attached; trader details, ratings and payouts stay in Spare Market.

parts.name: Bought assets work offline
parts.what: Fonts and assets bought in Spare Market are plain files that work offline for good, with no licence check-ins.

features.name: Make colour themes
features.does: Build, save and share colour themes and gradients from images, harmony rules or a phone camera.

parts.name: Colour theme maker
parts.what: A tool to build themes and gradients and save them to a library.

parts.name: Capture from a phone camera
parts.what: Pulls colours, patterns and shapes from the phone camera into a library.

areas.name: Spare Photo and Spare Paint: photo editing, compositing and painting
areas.summary: Edit and retouch photos, combine images, design graphics and paint by hand, all without harming the original. Replaces Photoshop and Fresco. Spare Paint is Spare Photo's brush engine in a touch-first layout.

features.name: Select exactly what they want
features.does: Select by shape, lasso, colour, edges, subject, sky or what is in focus, then refine hair and soft edges.

parts.name: Shape, lasso and wand selections
parts.what: Rectangle, ellipse, lasso, polygon, magnetic lasso and flood-fill selection tools.

parts.name: Colour range and focus area
parts.what: Selects by colour, tone, skin tones or the parts of a photo that are in focus.

parts.name: Subject, sky and object selection
parts.what: One-click selection of the subject, sky or a clicked object, using an open model that runs on the device.

parts.name: Refine edges
parts.what: A view to refine edges and hair, clean colour fringes and output the result as a mask.

parts.name: Quick mask and channels
parts.what: Paint a selection as a mask and save selections as channels.

features.name: Adjust colour and tone without harm
features.does: Use adjustment layers for levels, curves, exposure, hue, black and white, colour balance, gradient maps and more.

parts.name: Adjustment set
parts.what: The full set of tone and colour adjustments as GPU operations that stay editable.

parts.name: Adjustment panels
parts.what: Panels with live histograms, curves and adjusting by dragging on the image.

parts.name: Colour lookup tables
parts.what: Loads and saves LUTs in open formats such as .cube.

parts.name: Raw-style adjustments on any layer
parts.what: Applies Spare Raw's development controls to any layer as an editable filter.

features.name: Retouch and repair
features.does: Remove spots and objects, heal, clone and patch, with content-aware fill that needs no AI.

parts.name: Healing, clone and patch
parts.what: Spot healing, healing brush, clone and patch tools with sampling from any layer.

parts.name: Image method patent register
parts.what: Which published methods for fill, healing, patch matching, content-aware scale, auto-blend, image trace and denoise are free to use and which may be patented, kept as one register for every app.

parts.name: Content-aware fill
parts.what: Fills a selection from the rest of the image using a published patch-matching method.

parts.name: Red eye, dust and scratches
parts.what: Small automatic repairs for red eye, dust and scratches.

features.name: Combine images
features.does: Blend layers with blend modes and opacity, mask and clip them, and align and blend photos automatically.

parts.name: Blend modes and layer styles
parts.what: Every common blend mode and editable layer styles: shadow, glow, stroke, bevel and overlay.

parts.name: Layer, vector and clipping masks
parts.what: Pixel masks, vector masks and clipping groups with density and feather.

parts.name: Auto-align and auto-blend
parts.what: Lines up layers by their content and blends exposures or focus stacks.

assess: Does each app's area cover what you do every day in the Adobe app it replaces? What is missing from your own work?
Is "core" small enough that the first app (piece S08) could reach a usable release with the co-op's spare tokens?
Which parts could come from ArtCraft, Graphite, Penpot, OpenToonz or other permissively licensed projects instead of being built (piece S01)?
Is every Adobe file format handled only from a published specification, and which legal parts need a lawyer before work starts (piece S06)?
Is the studio core (document model, GPU pipeline, colour, text) truly shared by every app, or does any app quietly need its own?
Are the shared engines (render, 2D drawing, text, PDF, media) shared with Spare Arch, Spare Office and Spare Social rather than copied?

Does the at-cost model add up: what stays free, what do storage, AI and video processing cost a member each month, and does paying after use against a monthly cap keep the co-op from ever holding members' money?
Is the AI policy clear enough to build on: off by default, the member's choice of model, labelled, and never trained on members' work without consent (piece S07)?
Are accessibility, te reo Māori and offline work treated as core, not as extras for later?
Does anything in the demo or the map copy Adobe's interface designs, icons or names beyond saying what we replace?
Is the split with Spare Market right: Studio browses, installs and sends assets to sell, while listings, orders, tax, payouts and seller rules live in Spare Market?
Which large parts are the riskiest, and does each have a research or decision piece before building starts?
Are the hosting duties (illegal content, copyright notices, privacy) right-sized for a suite that is mostly local, with sharing on top?
Is the order of apps right: which three ship first, and which (3D, character animation) can wait?
Is anything here better left to an existing free tool than built by the co-op?
Does the demo show clearly what a person can do in each app on its first day?

The riskiest new research parts (browser build STU-A1-F1-P2, PSD fidelity STU-A2-F7-P6, EPS STU-A2-F7-P4, PDF content editing STU-A12-F3-P3, on-device model runtime STU-A16-F1-P5, audio latency STU-A11-F1-P4) have no work-board piece yet: which should become pieces first?

Several parts say they belong in the kit or a shared engine (per-member metering, the AI training consent register, organisation sign-on and audit log, the comment model, the office formats engine, the on-device model engine): should they move there now, before any program builds its own copy?
Is the native plugin host's exception to the WebAssembly-only plugin rule safe enough, and is desktop only acceptable for OpenFX, CLAP, LV2, VST 3 and Audio Unit plugins?
Is the co-op LGPL decision (STU-A20-F4-P5) made before any FFmpeg or raw decoding work starts?
